verdict.rationale: Vercel's first-party docs state that sandboxes run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs, so code runs without exposing production systems. Support for system-privileged workloads such as Docker, VPN clients and FUSE inside the sandbox fits a VM-level boundary rather than a shared-kernel container. However, the evidence offers only short marketing-level statements, with no depth on how the boundary works. Missing for 10: detailed isolation architecture or threat-model documentation (hypervisor, kernel separation, network egress controls), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the boundary.
